analysis.title: PBF Energy Inc. (PBF): First Take: Stronger Results Driven By West Coast Refining vs GS Model; Balance Sheet Moves to Net Cash Position
key_insights: PBF reported adjusted 3Q26 EPS of $12.78 vs GS estimate of $11.00 and FactSet consensus of $11.12, a $1.78 variance to the GS model.
West Coast refining drove the beat: gross margin of $38.64/bbl vs GS $24.36/bbl and implied operating income of $761 mn vs GS $373 mn, a $388 mn variance.
Mid-Continent also beat, with gross margin of $36.86/bbl vs GS $31.55/bbl and implied operating income of $438 mn vs GS $385 mn.

East Coast and Chalmette missed GS estimates. East Coast implied operating income was $746 mn vs $851 mn. Chalmette was $340 mn vs $430 mn, on gross margin of $27.61/bbl vs $31.80/bbl and opex of $7.16/bbl vs $6.00/bbl.
The company guided 4Q26 throughput to about 925-985 kbpd vs GS estimate of about 902 kbpd.
PBF reduced net debt by approximately 150% in 3Q and held $426 mn of net cash at quarter-end.
2026 capex guidance remains $825-$875 mn, excluding Martinez rebuild capital, and includes advance purchases of materials for the 2026 turnarounds rescheduled into 2027.
Costs vs the GS model: G&A was $127 mn vs $99 mn estimated, and interest expense was $27 mn vs $55 mn estimated.
GS rates PBF Neutral with a 6-month SOTP price target of $91, 24.2% above the $73.28 close on 28 Oct 2026.
GS expects the call to focus on refining margins by region, crude differentials, capital allocation priorities, and broader strategic initiatives.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and a 6-month SOTP target of $91 after the 3Q26 print. The target implies 24.2% upside to the $73.28 close.

risk_factors: Key risks named by GS relate to refining margins, operational execution, and capital returns.
